title: 12 Best Bibimbap in Jeonju Hanok Village
description: The best bibimbap in Jeonju Hanok Village — curated from Reddit reviews. Gogung, Hankookjib, Gajok Hoegwan, yukhoe bibimbap & more. Interactive map included.

places.name: Gogung (고궁)

redditQuotes.text: Starting with Gogung is a safe bet. In fact, in terms of bibimbap it is the safest. Gogung is THE place in Jeonju to eat bibimbap.
redditQuotes.source: — ZenKimchi food blog · Bibimbap in Jeonju: Where to Eat it

redditQuotes.text: I went to GoGung Suragan tonight for bibimbap and I was not disappointed.

places.verdict: The most famous bibimbap restaurant in Jeonju, period.

comparison.strengths: 3.8★ from 2,691 Google reviews · Traditional Bibimbap · Deokjin-gu, Jeonju (Main Branch)
comparison.why it made the list: The most famous bibimbap restaurant in Jeonju, period. Founded in 1996 as the successor to the legendary Han-Kuk-Kwan (est. 1966), Gogung serves bibimbap in the most traditional manner — brass bowl, sagol broth rice, 30+ fresh toppings. It's become a tourist destination in itself, with branches in Seoul's Myeong-dong. Yes, there will be a wait. Yes, it's worth it.
comparison.what to order: Gogung (고궁), located in Deokjin-gu, Jeonju, offers traditional bibimbap for ₩10,000–₩14,000 per person. Order the Jeonju traditional bibimbap (전주비빔밥) in the brass bowl, featuring rice cooked in sagol broth with over 30 toppings. For an extra ₩2,000, add the yukhoe (raw beef) version, and be sure not to skip the onion fried rice side.

redditQuotes.text: We had our taste of the Jeonju bibimbap at the Hankookjib Restaurant, one of the most popular places to have authentic bibimbap in the city. Located within the Jeonju Hanok Village, the restaurant has been operating since 1952 with their own family recipe.

Arrive before 5:30 PM to beat the dinner crowd.

The standard Jeonju bibimbap (₩11,000) with cooked beef is also excellent, and a vegetarian option is available.

places.name: Gajok Hoegwan (가족회관)

redditQuotes.text: In terms of fame and taste, Gajok Hwegwan follows closely on the heels of Gogung. Endorsed by the city, it is very conveniently located in the heart of the downtown area near the city's hanok village.
We ordered the Jeonju and Yukhoe bibimbap. Taste was ok, nothing spectacular and the protein provided was quite little. Our highlight was the gyeram jim.

places.verdict: The scrappy underdog to Gogung's polish.

comparison.strengths: Traditional Bibimbap · Downtown, near Hanok Village
comparison.why it made the list: The scrappy underdog to Gogung's polish. Open kitchen, cramped seating, fearsome ajummas running the show — it's gloriously authentic. The bibimbap is neck-and-neck with Gogung on taste, and some locals actually prefer it. Just don't stand in the kitchen's way or you'll get shoved aside. City-endorsed for a reason.
comparison.what to order: Gajok Hoegwan (가족회관), located downtown near Hanok Village, offers traditional bibimbap for ₩10,000–₩13,000 per person. Order the traditional Jeonju bibimbap to enjoy plentiful banchan and generous portions. You can watch the open kitchen where ajummas assemble your bowl with practiced speed; this restaurant is even endorsed by the city of Jeonju itself.

places.name: Hasukyeong Gamasot Bibimbap (하숙영 가마솥 비빔밥)

redditQuotes.text: Hasukyeong Gamasot Bibimbap: unique bibimbap in Jeonju — the iron pot cooking method gives it a completely different character from regular bibimbap.

comparison.strengths: 3.9★ from 1,540 Google reviews · Iron Pot Bibimbap · Hanok Village, Wansan-gu
comparison.why it made the list: The wildcard. While everyone else serves bibimbap in brass or stone, Hasukyeong uses a gamasot — a traditional iron cauldron that gives the rice an incredible depth of flavor. The nurungji crust at the bottom is chef's-kiss territory. If you've already had classic bibimbap and want something different, this is your move.
comparison.what to order: Hasukyeong Gamasot Bibimbap (하숙영 가마솥 비빔밥), located in Hanok Village, Wansan-gu, offers iron pot bibimbap for ₩10,000–₩12,000 per person. Order the gamasot (iron cauldron) bibimbap, cooked in a traditional Korean iron pot for an intense, slightly smoky rice flavor. The nurungji (scorched rice) at the bottom is the highlight, offering a unique twist on the classic.
